Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 86, verses 1–17:

It is Meccan.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

{1–4} Allah the Exalted says: {By the sky and the Tariq}. Then He explained the Tariq with His saying: {the piercing star}; that is, the bright one whose light pierces, so that it cleaves through the heavens, penetrates them, and becomes visible on the earth. The correct view is that it is a generic noun that includes all piercing stars. It has also been said that it is Saturn, which cleaves through and penetrates the seven heavens and is seen from them, and it was called Tariq because it "knocks" (yatruq) at night. The matter sworn to is His saying: {Indeed, over every soul there is a guardian}: it records over it its good and evil deeds, and it will be recompensed according to its recorded deeds.

{5–7} {So let man look at what he was created from}; that is, let him reflect upon his creation and his origin, for he was created {from a gushing fluid}: which is the semen, which {emerges from between the backbone and the ribs}. It is possible that this means from between the backbone of the man and the ribs ( tara'ib ) of the woman, which are her breasts; and it is possible that the intended meaning is the gushing fluid, which is the semen of the man, and that its place is what emerges from between his backbone and his ribs. Perhaps this is more likely, for it is only described as a gushing fluid that is sensed and whose gushing is observed, and it is the semen of the man. Likewise the word tara'ib, for it is used of the man, since the tara'ib of the man are in the position of the breasts of the female; so if the female had been intended, it would have said "from the backbone and the breasts" or the like. And Allah knows best.

{8–10} Then He who brought man into being from a gushing fluid that emerges from this difficult place is able to return him in the Hereafter and to restore him for resurrection, rising and recompense. It has been said that the meaning is that Allah is indeed able to return the fluid that was ejected from the backbone; and although this meaning is correct, it is not the intended meaning of the verse, which is why He said after it: {on the Day when secrets are tested}; that is, the hidden matters of the breasts will be tested, and what was in the hearts of good and evil will appear on the faces. As He said: {On the Day when some faces will turn white and some faces will turn black}. In this world many things are concealed and do not appear openly to people, but on the Day of Resurrection the righteousness of the righteous and the wickedness of the wicked will become manifest, and affairs will become public. And His saying: {Then he will have no power}; that is, from himself, by which he may defend himself, {nor any helper}: from outside, by whom he may be given victory. Thus this oath concerns the doers at the time of their deeds and at the time of their recompense.

{11–14} Then He swore a second oath concerning the truth of the Qur'an, saying: {By the sky which returns, and the earth which splits open}; that is, the sky returns with rain every year, and the earth splits open for vegetation, so that humans and animals live by it; and the sky also returns with the decrees and divine affairs at all times, and the earth splits open to release the dead. {Indeed, it}; that is, the Qur'an, {is a decisive word}; that is, a truth and a clear, evident sincerity, {and it is not a joke}; that is, it is earnest, not jest, and it is the word that distinguishes between groups and doctrines, and by which disputes are resolved.

{15–17} {Indeed they}; that is, those who deny the Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and the Qur'an, {are plotting a plot}: to repel the truth by their plotting and to support falsehood; {and I too am plotting a plot}: to make the truth manifest, even though the disbelievers dislike it, and to repel what they have brought of falsehood. From this it is known who is dominant, for the human being is weaker and more insignificant than to contend against the Mighty, the All-Knowing, in His plotting. {So give respite to the disbelievers; give them respite for a little while}; that is, briefly, for they will know the outcome of their affair when the punishment descends upon them.

It is finished. And praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds.

It is Meccan.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

{1–4} Allah the Exalted says: {By the sky and the Tariq}. Then He explained the Tariq with His saying: {the piercing star}; that is, the bright one whose light pierces, so that it cleaves through the heavens, penetrates them, and becomes visible on the earth. The correct view is that it is a generic noun that includes all piercing stars. It has also been said that it is Saturn, which cleaves through and penetrates the seven heavens and is seen from them, and it was called Tariq because it "knocks" (yatruq) at night. The matter sworn to is His saying: {Indeed, over every soul there is a guardian}: it records over it its good and evil deeds, and it will be recompensed according to its recorded deeds.

{5–7} {So let man look at what he was created from}; that is, let him reflect upon his creation and his origin, for he was created {from a gushing fluid}: which is the semen, which {emerges from between the backbone and the ribs}. It is possible that this means from between the backbone of the man and the ribs ( tara'ib ) of the woman, which are her breasts; and it is possible that the intended meaning is the gushing fluid, which is the semen of the man, and that its place is what emerges from between his backbone and his ribs. Perhaps this is more likely, for it is only described as a gushing fluid that is sensed and whose gushing is observed, and it is the semen of the man. Likewise the word tara'ib, for it is used of the man, since the tara'ib of the man are in the position of the breasts of the female; so if the female had been intended, it would have said "from the backbone and the breasts" or the like. And Allah knows best.

It has been said that the meaning is that Allah is indeed able to return the fluid that was ejected from the backbone; and although this meaning is correct, it is not the intended meaning of the verse, which is why He said after it: {on the Day when secrets are tested}; that is, the hidden matters of the breasts will be tested, and what was in the hearts of good and evil will appear on the faces. {15–17} {Indeed they}; that is, those who deny the Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and the Qur'an, {are plotting a plot}: to repel the truth by their plotting and to support falsehood; {and I too am plotting a plot}: to make the truth manifest, even though the disbelievers dislike it, and to repel what they have brought of falsehood. From this it is known who is dominant, for the human being is weaker and more insignificant than to contend against the Mighty, the All-Knowing, in His plotting. {So give respite to the disbelievers; give them respite for a little while}; that is, briefly, for they will know the outcome of their affair when the punishment descends upon them.

It is finished. And praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds.
